programme.desc: Rodiles provoca una fuga masiva, anuncia el fin de Las Dunas y compensa la lealtad de La Puma, liberándola. Guillotina hiere de bala al comandante David.

programme.title: Enemigo íntimo
programme.desc: A la cabeza de su nuevo cártel, Los Jinetes Jíbaros, Guillotina jura degollar a Nemesio, a Roxana y a Daniel. Rodiles advierte a Laborde que no soportaría su traición. Le disparan a Fermín.

programme.title: Falsa identidad
programme.desc: Llega la hora de que Gavino ajuste cuentas con Joselito para que pague por su deslealtad. El capo lo hace sufrir al máximo y disfruta su destrucción. Nuria pasa por un momento traumático.

programme.title: Falsa identidad
programme.desc: Gavino tiene la ubicación de Circe y le deja un mensaje para que ella entienda que él mueve los hilos y quien se atreva a desafiarlo, pagará con su vida. Diego pide inmunidad para Isabel y él.

programme.title: 12 corazones
programme.desc: Un programa de concurso picante, ligero y excitante el cual busca formar una o varias parejas entre los participantes que se gusten y se sientan atraídos.

programme.title: Caso cerrado
programme.sub-title: Entrenador embaraza a menor; Ofensa en el funeral
programme.desc: Manuel tuvo una relación legal con una menor de edad, pero lo denuncian por entrar a su email sin permiso. Demandan a una profesora por resaltar lo peor de su alumno durante el funeral.

programme.title: Caso cerrado
programme.sub-title: José, el enano; Problema de niños
programme.desc: Lourdes está casada con José, ella le exige que acepte su discapacidad, pero él se niega porque se siente sano y fuerte. Dos niñas se enfrentan por unos "tickets" para ir a Euro Disney en París.

programme.title: Caso cerrado
programme.sub-title: Aire mortal; El emú y la esmeralda
programme.desc: Ernesto sufre las consecuencias de tener un vecino obsesionado con las armas. Además, Lily exige que un emú sea operado porque se tragó la esmeralda que estaba en su anillo de matrimonio.

programme.title: Caso cerrado
programme.sub-title: Radio de la frontera; Calientes, pero quietos
programme.desc: Valentina y Juan tienen un programa radial sin audiencia, cuando él cambia el enfoque pone en peligro a los inmigrantes indocumentados. Los maniquíes semidesnudos de Cairo molestan a su vecina.

programme.title: Enemigo íntimo
programme.desc: Rodiles provoca una fuga masiva, anuncia el fin de Las Dunas y compensa la lealtad de La Puma, liberándola. Guillotina hiere de bala al comandante David.

programme.title: Enemigo íntimo
programme.desc: A la cabeza de su nuevo cártel, Los Jinetes Jíbaros, Guillotina jura degollar a Nemesio, a Roxana y a Daniel. Rodiles advierte a Laborde que no soportaría su traición. Le disparan a Fermín.

programme.title: 100 días para enamorarnos
programme.desc: En su debut, Lobo es un triunfador y Constanza queda encandilada. Plutarco firma el contrato para representar a Ramírez legalmente en su divorcio. Cuesta los enfrenta por separado.

programme.title: 100 días para enamorarnos
programme.desc: El padre de Constanza va a parar al hospital. Plutarco y Lobo compiten por consolarla en este asunto, que Cuesta lo considera de carácter familiar. Se da un acalorado cruce de palabras.

programme.title: Juego de villanos
programme.desc: Dieciocho villanos icónicos compiten por el título de "El Emperador de los Villanos" y 200 mil dólares. Entre desafíos, inmunidades, alianzas y traiciones, solo uno alcanza la cima.

programme.title: Falsa identidad
programme.desc: Llega la hora de que Gavino ajuste cuentas con Joselito para que pague por su deslealtad. El capo lo hace sufrir al máximo y disfruta su destrucción. Nuria pasa por un momento traumático.

programme.title: Falsa identidad
programme.desc: Gavino tiene la ubicación de Circe y le deja un mensaje para que ella entienda que él mueve los hilos y quien se atreva a desafiarlo, pagará con su vida. Diego pide inmunidad para Isabel y él.

programme.title: Eva la trailera
programme.desc: Eva creía que lo tenía todo en la vida: un buen marido, una familia perfecta y una situación económica estable. Pero entonces el destino le arroja una serie de obstáculos y traiciones que la llevan al borde de precipicio.

programme.title: Eva la trailera
programme.desc: Eva creía que lo tenía todo en la vida: un buen marido, una familia perfecta y una situación económica estable. Pero entonces el destino le arroja una serie de obstáculos y traiciones que la llevan al borde de precipicio.

programme.title: Caso cerrado
programme.desc: Yasyky y Yokymata viven como si estuvieran en una historia de Manga y piensan mudarse a Japón. Por otro lado, Mauricio quiere que su esposa deje las redes sociales porque afectan su matrimonio.

programme.title: Caso cerrado
programme.sub-title: Dinero tragado, dinero cagado; Chupa piernas
programme.desc: Tayra se traga casi 10 mil dólares para protegerlos de unos traficantes, luego los evacua y paga sus gastos médicos. César pone al niño a lamer piernas de mujeres porque su saliva es curativa.

programme.title: Super Password
programme.desc: Like the 1960s version, two contestants, each teamed with a celebrity partner, compete in a word-association game. The team with the most points at the end of the round gets to go on to a fast-paced bonus round called Cashword.

programme.title: Celebrity Name Game
programme.desc: Early on in game shows, when stars took part, they aided players -- to guess secret words on "Password," for instance. Now they're helping them guess names of VIPs in host Craig Ferguson's four-round competition set in a party atmosphere. The celebrity/contestant pairs must identify the famous -- actors, athletes, politicians, cartoon characters, etc. -- based on improvised clues for a chance to win $20,000. The celebrity connection extends behind the cameras; actors Courteney Cox and David Arquette are among executive producers of a show based on board game "Identity Crisis.".

programme.title: Card Sharks
programme.desc: This show from legendary Mark Goodson-Bill Todman Productions features two contestants trying to predict answers to survey questions for the opportunity to play a game with oversized playing cards for a chance to win cash. One contestant guesses how many people (out of 100) gave a certain answer to a question and the other contestant then guesses if the number is higher or lower than the opponent's guess. The winning contestant then faces a row of cards and must determine if each succeeding card is higher or lower than the one that precedes it. The contestant who wins two out of three games wins the match and plays the bonus round, called Money Cards. The Money Cards round is similar to the card game in the main game but with three levels of cards instead of one row. The contestant is given $200 at the beginning of Money Cards and wagers any or all of that money when guessing if the cards will be higher or lower than the previous one. A perfect round could earn the contestant $28,800.

programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." The two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. A trio of models presents the prizes.

programme.title: CBS News Sunday Morning
programme.desc: The sparkling notes of a trumpet fanfare and the familiar logo of the sun alert viewers that it's time for CBS's Sunday morning staple. Journalist Jane Pauley helms the show, taking over hosting duties from Charles Osgood, who spent 22 years on the job. A morning talk show, this program airs at a different pace and focuses much of its attention on the performing arts. After a quick update of the day's news and national weather, correspondents offer longer-length segments on a variety of topics, from architecture to ballet to music to pop culture to politics.

As Halloween descends upon Laurie's peaceful community, a feeling of dread weighs upon her -- with good reason.

The Princeton-educated Gilbert became a tabloid obsession when he shot his father after his $1,000 allowance was cut off. But in this unique installment of Interview With a Killer, Gilbert appears to be a far cry from his once golden upbringing. Host David Scott explores his long history of mental illness and the privileged pressure cooker that shaped his downfall.

programme.title: Interview With a Killer
programme.desc: In 2013, the small city of Weatherford, Texas was rocked by the brutal slaying of local son, JD Doss. The murder weapon? A pickaxe. The murderer? His close friend, 24-year-old Nicholas Camfield. In a shocking twist, Camfield not only killed his victim by repeatedly striking him in the head, he also mutilated, scalped, and defiled his body over the course of days. In one of David Scott's most shocking interviews, Camfield gives a glimpse inside his deranged, murderous mind.

programme.title: Interview With a Killer
programme.desc: She's one of the most camera-friendly killers in true crime history. A glamorous Texas social climber turned convicted black widow. Celeste Beard Johnson has done many television interviews, flashing a smile as she proclaims her innocence and pleads for sympathy. But she's never been questioned by David Scott. And this interview is unlike any that she's ever done. In this special episode of Interview With a Killer, host David Scott reveals the real Celeste - cunning, calculating, and deadly.

programme.title: What Would You Do?
programme.desc: Using hidden cameras, host John Quiñones observes and comments on how ordinary people behave when they are confronted with dilemmas that require them either to take action or to walk by and mind their own business. Various scenarios are created that force people to make split-second -- and often surprising -- decisions, and variations of the situation (such as changing the genders, races or clothing of the people involved) are often featured to see if different reactions are elicited. Examples of situations on the show include a waitress being harassed by her boss, and a drunken valet trying to park cars.
A college student's murder haunts a community for years; with the verdict just in, jurors, investigators and friends reveal new details.

But after Dorothy's fiancé (George Meeker) proclaims his love for another woman, she wonders if any man can love her for more than her money. Still disguised as a secretary, Dorothy falls for Tony (Joel McCrea) and puts him through a series of tests to prove his affections.

programme.desc: The staggeringly wealthy Norah Hunter (Laraine Day), a shipyard owner, too often finds herself the romantic target of gold-digging men. To attract a suitor whose main interest is not money, she changes places with her secretary, Sylvia Lockwood (Marsha Hunt), and assumes the role of a young working woman. However, she then falls for recuperating fighter pilot Anthony Travis (Alan Marshal), who, in turn, is madly in love with Sylvia -- or, perhaps, with the millions he thinks she has.

programme.title: Sun Valley Serenade
programme.desc: As a surefire way to receive good press, bandleader Phil Corey (Glenn Miller) and his ensemble decide to adopt a war refugee. When it turns out that their adoptee isn't a child, but a pretty Scandinavian woman named Karen Benson (Sonja Henie), it leads to a flirtatious relationship with the group's pianist, Ted Scott (John Payne), who is already involved with singer Vivian Dawn (Lynn Bari). As the band heads to snowy Idaho for a gig, romantic drama, skiing, ice skating and musical numbers ensue.

programme.title: Orchestra Wives
programme.desc: When a touring swing band arrives in her small town, Connie Ward (Ann Rutherford) falls hard for trumpeter Bill Abbot (George Montgomery) and decides to marry him on a whim -- since the band is leaving as quickly as it arrived. Quite unprepared for her new lifestyle, Connie struggles to adjust to the constant travel from one town to another, and also to the pettiness of the other musicians' wives. Eventually, the marriage and the band break up, but Bill is determined to make it all right again.

programme.title: Birth of the Blues

However, the Basin Street Hotshots are rejected from several venues for playing "black" jazz, until singer Betty Lou Cobb (Mary Martin) insists they be hired as her backup band. The band finds success until Jeff and Memphis fall out over Betty Lou, then get entangled with gangster Blackie (J. Carrol Naish).

programme.title: Girl Crazy

When Ginger, whose family runs the all-male college, explains that the school has money troubles, creative Danny puts together a big fundraiser. The event highlights their song-and-dance skills and also cements their bond.

programme.title: Strike Up the Band

Jimmy and his friends decide to put on an epic student play to raise the funds they need, but a sudden illness threatens to cost the band their chance.

programme.title: Pot o' Gold

Before he gets there, he befriends an Irish family who happens to be his uncle's worst enemy because of their love for music and in-house band that constantly practices. Soon, Jimmy finds himself trying to help the band by getting them gigs and trying to reconcile the family with his uncle, an avid music-hater.

programme.title: God Is My Co-Pilot

Scott is so good that Chennault gives him his wish -- he will fly combat missions with the Tigers.

programme.title: El señor de los cielos
programme.desc: Al final de la década de los ochentas, en el negocio ilícito más lucrativo de la época, "el oro blanco", las rutas de las Bahamas y Florida, ya no son tan viables para el transporte de la cocaína; la persecución de los miembros de los carteles colombianos y su guerra entre ellos mismos se intensifica, generando que estos bandidos sean extraditados, encarcelados en su país o asesinados. Algunos son condenados al encierro voluntario, escondidos en algún rincón para evitar su captura, por cuenta de las fuerzas armadas o de sus enemigos. El negocio cambia y es cuando aparece Amado Carrillo Fuentes "El Señor de los Cielos" que en forma muy discreta se dedica al transporte del producto que proveen los narcotraficantes colombianos restantes, convirtiéndose en el narcotraficante más poderoso de los cuatro carteles que operan en México: el de Juárez, el del Golfo, el de Sinaloa y el de Tijuana. Su historia se devela en este drama cargado de acción y giros inusitados.
